Maladaptive Strategies.value: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed

Memory.value: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together

Negative Appraisals.value: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed

vignette: Amir's eyes would often scan the room, his gaze darting from one face to another, searching for potential threats. It was a habit he'd developed over the past year, ever since the night his wife, Fatima, had attacked him in their home. The physical abuse had left him with more than just bruises - it had shattered his sense of trust and security. The event itself was still etched vividly in his mind. He remembered the darkness of the room, the sound of Fatima's voice raised in anger, and the feeling of being trapped and helpless. Even now, when he found himself in dark spaces or walked through certain physical locations that reminded him of their home, Amir would feel a wave of anxiety wash over him. The memories came flooding back without warning - the sound of Fatima's screams, the feeling of her hands around his throat. To cope with these triggers, Amir had started to avoid places that reminded him of the event, including their old neighborhood and even certain restaurants they used to frequent. He'd also become hypervigilant towards people, always on the lookout for potential dangers. This constant state of alertness was exhausting, but Amir felt it was necessary - after all, he had been betrayed by someone he trusted. The sound of helicopters or aircraft overhead would also send him spiraling back to that night. He remembered hearing a helicopter flying low over their neighborhood during the attack, and now the sound would instantly transport him back to that moment. When this happened, Amir's mind would fill with disconnected pieces of memories - fragmented images and sounds that didn't quite fit together. Amir had also started wearing concealing clothing, hoping to avoid drawing attention to himself. He felt like he was walking around with a neon sign on his head, advertising his vulnerability to the world. This sense of shame and self-blame was suffocating him - Amir had come to believe that the event happened because of some flaw in his own character. As a community organizer, Amir's work required him to be out in public, meeting new people and building relationships. But since the attack, he'd found it increasingly difficult to connect with others. He felt like he was living in a constant state of fear, always looking over his shoulder, waiting for the next shoe to drop. Fatima had left him shortly after the attack, but Amir's sense of betrayal lingered. He couldn't shake the feeling that he'd somehow deserved what happened to him - that it was all because of who he was as a person. This shattered his long-held beliefs about the world being a just and fair place. It wasn't until Amir started noticing the toll this was taking on his relationships with friends and family that he realized he needed help. His wife, Fatima's sister, had been trying to get him to see a therapist for months, but Amir had resisted. Now, as he sat in his small apartment, surrounded by reminders of a life he used to know, he knew it was time to confront the demons that haunted him. Amir's biggest fear was that he'd never be able to escape the memories of that night - that they'd continue to haunt him forever. But what frightened him most was losing himself completely in this sea of anxiety and self-doubt. He hoped that with therapy, he could begin to rebuild his shattered sense of self and find a way to live without being constantly terrorized by his own memories.
